questions.question: If a chair is sold at a discount of 20%, then there is a profit of 20%. If the chair is sold at a discount of 30%, then what will be the profit?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Marked Price (MP)** = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 20) : (100 + 20) = 80 : 120 = 2 : 3

New **Selling Price (SP)** at 30% discount = MP × 70% = 3 × 0.7 = 2.1 units

New **Profit Percentage** = [(2.1 − 2) ÷ 2] × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Discount** = 20% | Initial **Profit** = 20%

New **Discount** = 30%

**Formula Used:**

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/576435e91d58e47c2e302623cc417ff055cb07394145d50f3bb0ff521ede0e17.png] 

⇒ MP ÷ CP = (100 + 20) ÷ (100 − 20)

⇒ MP ÷ CP = 120 ÷ 80 = 3 ÷ 2

⇒ Let **CP** = ₹200 and **MP** = ₹300

⇒ New **Discount** = 30% of ₹300 = ₹90

⇒ New **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹300 − ₹90 = ₹210

⇒ New **Profit** = ₹210 − ₹200 = ₹10

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (₹10 ÷ ₹200) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation between CP and MP

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is given by MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Markup Percentage

Markup% is the percentage by which MP is greater than CP: Markup% = [(Profit + Discount) ÷ (100 − Discount)] × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

questions.question: If a boy goes from his home to his school at a speed of 40 km/h, he reaches 10 minutes early. If he goes at a speed of 35 km/h, he reaches 5 minutes late. What will be the time taken for the journey at a speed of 35 km/h?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio of speeds** is S₁ : S₂ = 40 : 35 = 8 : 7.

Since the **distance** between home and school is **constant**, the **time ratio** is the inverse of the speed ratio: T₁ : T₂ = 7 : 8.

The **total difference in time** between being early and late is 10 + 5 = 15 min.

In the ratio, the difference (8 − 7) = 1 unit → 15 min.

Therefore, the **time taken at 35 km/h** (which corresponds to 8 units) = 8 × 15 = 120 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Initial speed** (S₁) = 40 km/h (reaches 10 min early)

**Reduced speed** (S₂) = 35 km/h (reaches 5 min late)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2b3c1820f0d9979068a3b8a80b67d32d992c1f77330d8dfac445b5d0953eee3.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance (D) = [ (S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ − S₂) ] × ΔT

Where ΔT is the **total time difference** in hours.

**Calculations:**

⇒ ΔT = (10 + 5) min = 15 min = 15/60 hours = 1/4 hours

⇒ D = [ (40 × 35) ÷ (40 − 35) ] × (1/4)

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Coriolis force:

 
 
• ​The rotation of the earth about its axis affects the direction of the wind and this force is called the Coriolis force.
 
• It is directly proportional to the angle of latitude.
 
• It deflects the wind to the left direction in the southern hemisphere and the right direction in the northern hemisphere.
 
• Coriolis force deflects surface currents At an angle of about 45 degrees to the wind-to the right in the Northern Hemisphere, left in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• It is maximum at the poles and is absent at the equator.
 
• The force acts perpendicular to the pressure gradient force.
 
• The Coriolis force is zero at the equator and the wind blows perpendicular to the isobars.
 
• Major surface ocean currents in the open ocean, however, are set in motion by the wind, which drags on the surface of the water as it blows. The winds pull surface water with them, creating currents. As these currents flow westward, the Coriolis effect, a force that results from the rotation of the Earth, deflects them.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5d309a4703fb6ee156ad105ab1a4035194d68085364f2cbfe08fb9b483d4cbf.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7b7533525eae5e3efa4188d7f04db943960c29a341ef0f6287d86dbaabeb3bf.png] 

 
• **Tidal Waves - **

 
 
• The strongest force responsible for the phenomenon of tides is the Gravitational force of the moon.
 
• The gra vitational pulls between the earth, moon, and sun dictate the tides. The moon, however, influences tides the most.
 
• When two masses are placed at some distance to each other then it applies force on each other. This force is called gravitational force.
 
• Newton’s law of gravitation: According to this law- When two objects having some masses are placed at a certain distance then the gravitational force is directly proportional to the product of masses and it is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• The moon and sun are the main reason for the rising and falling of ocean tides.
 
• As the moon is closer to earth so the gravitational pull of the moon is more than that of the gravitational pull of the sun. So the tidal effect of the moon is more than that of the sun.
 
• Hence the strongest reason for Tidal waves or ocean waves in the sea is the Gravitational effect of the Moon.
 
 
 
• **Wind -**
 
 
• The **wind blows** because of **differences in air pressure** from one location to another.
 
• The **wind blows** from** areas of high pressure** toward** areas of low pressure**. 
 
• If the **high-pressure area** is very close to** the low-pressure area**, or if the** pressure difference** is very great, the** wind** can** blow very fast**.
 
• **Air pressure** depends on the **density of the air**, or how close together its** molecules **are.
 
• **Air lower** in the **atmosphere** is denser than the **air** above, so** air pressure down low is greater than air pressure higher up.**
 
• **Temperature also makes changes in air pressure.**
 
• In **cold air,** the **molecules **are more closely packed together than in **warm air**, so** cold air **is **denser** than **warm air**.
 
• Since** warm air** is less dense and creates less **air pressure**, it** will rise**; **cold air** is denser and creates** greater air pressure**, and so it will **sink**.
 
• When** warm air rises**, **cooler air** will often move in to replace it, so wind often moves from areas where it's colder to areas where it's **warmer.**
 
• The greater the difference between the **high** and **low pressure** or the **shorter** the distance between the high and **low-pressure areas**, the** faster** the **wind will blow**.
 
• **Wind** also** blows** faster if there's nothing in its way, so winds are usually **stronger over oceans** or **flat ground**.
 
• **Meteorologists** can** forecast **the speed and direction of the wind by **measuring air pressure** with a **barometer**.

questions.question: Push and pull factors are associated with which component of the population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Migration.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International migration** is the outcome of a** mix of forces that push people** away from their countries of origin and** entice them t**o a particular destination country.
 
• **Push factors **can include
 
 
• **armed conflict, **
 
• **natural disasters,**
 
• the lack of** job opportunities,**
 
• the possession of** economic and cultural capital,**
 
• a family **break up** or
 
• **dissatisfaction** with one’s own life and surroundings
 
 
 
• **Pull factors** can often be the polar opposites of the push factors, i.e.
 
 
• **greater security,**
 
• better** job opportunities** or
 
• the prospect of a more **exciting life.**
 
 
 
• However, some pull factors, such as closeness to a **push factor or the presence of family or community members **in the destination nation, do not immediately correlate with push factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Death rate:**

 
 
• A** population's mortality rate **is often known as death rate.
 
• It is a measurement of the **number of deaths** within that** population per unit of time**, scaled to that population's size.
 
 
 
• **Birth rate:**
 
 
• The number of babies born in a population in a specific period of time is known as the birth rate.
